beliefs.practice: Use a single, long-lived MongoClient instance per process and reuse it for all requests (do not open a new client per request). Configure maxPoolSize to a reasonable value (e.g., 50) and set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS to avoid blocking callers.
Keep the DocumentDB connection URI/credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment variables (or from a config file that is not checked in). Never log the full URI or secrets.

Prefer managed secret storage for production: store DB credentials in Azure Key Vault and fetch them at runtime, or use a deployment secret mechanism. Do not embed primary keys in code or sample fixtures.
Enable TLS/SSL on the client connection and enforce server certificate validation; restrict cluster access with firewall rules or VNet/IP allow lists so only app hosts can reach the cluster.

Use a dedicated database and collections for this sample (sample_retail_13) and avoid reading or modifying other databases. Use collection names that separate product documents from embedding/chunk documents (e.g., products, product_chunks).

Design document schema for retrieval: store each chunk with fields {product_id, chunk_id, text, embedding: <float array>, length, source, metadata: {...}} so you can filter on metadata and compute scores without re-reading product docs.

Keep embedding vectors fixed-dimension and use a consistent dtype (e.g., float32). Add a metadata field that records the embedding dimension and model name to detect mismatches before indexing/queries.

Create a scalar/index on commonly filtered fields such as product_id and any category/tags used for filtering, and create a text index for fallback keyword matching on chunk text (e.g., db.product_chunks.createIndex({text: 'text'})).

When enabling a vector index, specify the same distance metric used at query time (cosine/inner_product or euclidean) and configure index parameters appropriate for the size (e.g., HNSW efConstruction/efSearch values or IVF nlist). Ensure the vector index dimension matches stored vectors.

If vector indexing or vector search configuration tools are needed, verify index creation with the cluster management tooling (MCP) and inspect query plans; have fallback text/search code path if vector index isn't present.

Implement exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors (network timeouts, 5xx server errors). For writes that must be retried, ensure idempotency (use upserts or include a client-generated idempotency token field).

Bulk-load seeding operations in moderate-sized batches (e.g., 500–1000 documents per insert_many) and set ordered=False so a single bad document doesn't fail the whole batch. Monitor for request size and document size limits.

Limit document size (keep chunks well under platform limits ~16MB) and prefer smaller chunk sizes with overlap tuned for both retrieval quality and token budget (e.g., 500–1000 tokens with 10–20% overlap).

For RAG prompt engineering: retrieve top-N (e.g., 5) chunks, deduplicate and rank by combined vector score + metadata score, then truncate or select spans to ensure the assembled context fits the LLM token limit.
Store provenance metadata with each chunk (source doc id, chunk index, URL, timestamp) so generated answers can cite sources and allow traceability/auditing of RAG outputs.
When vector indexes are unavailable, implement a deterministic fallback to text search (text index and score by textScore) and clearly signal to the app/logs that vector path was not used.
Monitor index usage and query performance (slow queries, index misses) and maintain an automated test that validates retrieval latency and recall for a small set of canonical queries after seeding.

Limit client-side scanning by applying server-side filters before computing embeddings/similarity (e.g., filter by product category or availability) to reduce vector-search cost and improve precision.

Use consistent serialization for vectors (store as dense arrays of numbers in a single field) and avoid storing vectors as nested documents or strings; index the array field as the vector index target.
Rotate/roll keys periodically and avoid using primary/master key in long-lived deployments. If using read-only app credentials, restrict permissions to the required database/collections.
